creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Held-Out Assessment
Evaluation Protocol
Leakage
Predictive Fidelity
description: A p5.js timeline of one synthetic learner's xAPI statements in which learners drag a forecast cutoff, see which practice answers and exposure events may feed a BKT forecast, and watch leaked held-out answers inflate a mock cohort accuracy from 0.705 to 0.910.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Held-out assessments and leakage in forecast evaluation
learningObjectives: Distinguish statements that may legitimately feed a forecast from those that leak the held-out assessment, by placing a forecast cutoff on a learner's timeline and judging each statement.
prerequisites: BKT forecast of a correct next answer

accessibility.keyboardNotes: Left and right arrow keys move the forecast cutoff between statements.
accessibility.colorBlindSafePalette: Okabe-Ito, with a distinct marker shape per statement type

controls.label: Forecast cutoff line (drag, click in the timeline, or arrow keys)
Allow the model to see assessment answers

simulation.modelType: Rule-based evidence window with a BKT forecast
variables: forecast of a correct held-out answer
equations: Forecast = P(L) (1 - ps) + (1 - P(L)) pg after the BKT update over the answers in use (L0 0.30, pt 0.15, pg 0.20, ps 0.10)
assumptions: The learner's timeline is hand-written and synthetic.

Mock accuracies come from the Chapter 19 synthetic cohort (200 learners, seed 19): 0.365, 0.530, 0.660, 0.685 and 0.705 with 0 to 4 practice answers, and 0.910 when the held-out answer leaks into the forecast.
Exposure events carry no right or wrong answer and do not change the BKT forecast.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge-then-check with a deliberate failure case
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Timeline explorer with a draggable boundary
keyQuestions: Which statements may feed a forecast of the held-out answer?
Why is a statement produced after the assessment a leak even if it is a practice answer?
Why is an accuracy computed with leaked statements not evidence?
commonMisconceptions: Using every statement a learner produced gives the most honest forecast.
Only the assessment answer itself can leak; later practice or feedback views cannot.
A higher accuracy always means a better model.
assessmentOpportunities: Mark the latest valid forecast cutoff on a new timeline.
List the statements that leak when the cutoff moves past the assessment.
